To express the quadratic function \(3 x^2 + x - 4\) in vertex form \(a(x - h)^2 + k\), we
first complete the square. We factor out the coefficient of \(x^2\): \(3(x^2 +
\frac{1}{3}x) - 4\). Next, we complete the square inside the parentheses: \(x^2 +
\frac{1}{3}x = \left(x + \frac{1}{6}\right)^2 - \frac{1}{36}\). Thus, we rewrite the
function as \(3\left(\left(x + \frac{1}{6}\right)^2 - \frac{1}{36}\right) - 4\), which
simplifies to \(3\left(x + \frac{1}{6}\right)^2 - \frac{49}{12}\). In this vertex form,
\(k = -\frac{49}{12}\) represents the minimum value of the function, indicating the lowest
point on the graph, and it is significant as it determines the vertical position of the
vertex, influencing the overall shape and direction of the parabola.
